paper.title: Myocardial Hypertrophic Preconditioning Attenuates Cardiomyocyte Hypertrophy and Slows Progression to Heart Failure Through Upregulation of S100A8/A9

challenge_geometry.withdrawal: aortic debanding for 4 days or 1 week
challenge_geometry.same_class_rechallenge: re-TAC followed by 1 or 6 weeks of renewed pressure overload
challenge_geometry.load_equivalence_control: re-TAC groups were compared with sustained TAC under similar pressure-overload measurements

why_H3a_is_supported: The same tissue is exposed to pressure overload, unloaded, and then exposed again to the same class of pressure overload; subsequent remodeling is blunted relative to naive sustained-pressure controls despite renewed load.

why_H3b_is_not_admitted.reason: The first TAC episode is deliberately short and is described as compensatory hypertrophic preconditioning. Significant hypertrophy is present, but the root does not directly establish a mature pathological fibrotic/mechanical lock before debanding. Therefore resistance on re-TAC cannot be represented as reversal and rewriting of an already-established mature fibrotic lock.

mechanical_exit_coupling.reason: The root does not provide lineage-resolved activated-fibroblast EXIT mode across load withdrawal and rechallenge.

claim_ceiling.supported: Tissue-level cardiac mechanical-history dependence can make the heart more resistant to a later pressure-overload challenge.
not_supported: durable rewrite after a mature fibrotic lock
